articles.excerpt: Introduction SOCKS5 proxies have become essential tools for developers, marketers, and businesses handling sensitive online operations. Unlike HTTP proxies that only work with web traffic, SOCKS5 (Soc…
articles.body: Introduction SOCKS5 proxies have become essential tools for developers, marketers, and businesses handling sensitive online operations. Unlike HTTP proxies that only work with web traffic, SOCKS5 (Socket Secure version 5) operates at the transport layer, supporting any TCP or UDP protocol. This makes them incredibly versatile for web scraping, secure browsing, load testing, and geolocation-specific tasks. If you're researching proxy solutions, you've likely encountered confusing terminology, exaggerated claims, and misleading pricing. This guide cuts through the noise and explains what SOCKS5 proxies actually do, when you should use them, and which providers deliver genuine value. How SOCKS5 Proxies Work SOCKS5 proxies act as intermediaries between your application and the internet.

Well, as the saying goes, luck eventually does run out. I’ve had my Pixel 11 Pro for just five days, and it’s already a brick. A couple of days into my time with the Pixel 11 Pro (in the gorgeous Canyon colorway), I decided to do a factory reset and a fresh setup instead of copying over all my data from my previous phone, and here we are.

We describe the task in Markdown, declare the tools and boundaries in front matter, then compile that source into an ordinary GitHub Actions workflow. articles.title: Baklava: Generate API Documentation and Type-Safe Clients from Scala Routing Tests
articles.excerpt: API documentation has a reliability problem. The code gets updated; the OpenAPI spec gets forgotten. The spec gets updated; the TypeScript client doesn't regenerate. By the time an enterprise client a…
articles.body: API documentation has a reliability problem. The code gets updated; the OpenAPI spec gets forgotten. The spec gets updated; the TypeScript client doesn't regenerate. By the time an enterprise client asks for your API contract, the document you hand them describes a system that no longer exists. Baklava, an open-source library by Iterators , solves this structurally: documentation is generated from the tests that verify your actual API behaviour, so it cannot drift. The problem Documentation drift is the default state of any API that lives long enough. The causes are well-understood: docs and code are maintained separately, documentation updates require extra discipline at every PR, and no automated check catches a route signature change that wasn't reflected in the OpenAPI file.

articles.title: Why your hreflang tags are being ignored
articles.excerpt: Originally published on the WeLocale blog. Most SEO work is a matter of degree. You improve a title, you gain a little. hreflang is not like that. It either forms a valid set that search engines act o…
articles.body: Originally published on the WeLocale blog . Most SEO work is a matter of degree. You improve a title, you gain a little. hreflang is not like that. It either forms a valid set that search engines act on, or it does nothing at all, and the failure is completely silent. No warning, no penalty, no message in Search Console telling you the tags you carefully added are being discarded. We build a translation widget, which means we generate hreflang tags for other people's sites. This post is what we have learned about why they get ignored, including the parts where our own approach has real limits. The rule that breaks most setups hreflang is not a property of a page. It is a property of a set of pages, and every page in that set has to agree.

A zero-cost invoice hides the most expensive resource in your workflow: your own attention. articles.excerpt: It's a small fix, but a welcome one for anyone who relies on voice alarms daily.
articles.body: TL;DR Some Google Home devices stopped setting alarms via voice command for several days. The bug hit both Google Assistant and Gemini for Home, affecting Nest speakers, displays, and even third-party devices like Lenovo smart displays. Google has confirmed the fix, and our own testing shows alarms are setting and triggering correctly again. Google Home has had a busy August, with Google rolling out several updates that make Gemini for Home smarter and add new capabilities to its smart home platform. But amid all those improvements, something as basic as setting an alarm suddenly stopped working for some users. Thankfully, Google has now confirmed that the issue affecting Nest and other Gemini-powered smart home devices has been fixed.

articles.title: The Pixel 11 Pro’s camera flash is a ‘LoLight’ thanks to HiLight
articles.excerpt: Users complain that the Pixel 11 Pro's camera flash is a big downgrade over other phones, and HiLight could be to blame here.
articles.body: Credit: Sanuj Bhatia / Android Authority TL;DR Reddit users report that the Google Pixel 11 Pro’s camera flash is significantly weaker than that of older Pixels and competitors. Our preliminary testing here at Android Authority shows the Pixel 11 Pro XL torch mode registered 89 lux compared to 123 lux on the Pixel 10 Pro XL. The physical diffuser added to the camera visor for the new HiLight LED array is likely the cause of the softer beam. Google’s new Pixel 11 Pro series introduces HiLight , a small array of ambient LEDs around the camera flash that give you some bits of information without requiring you to turn over or unlock your phone. Google ended up severely limiting HiLight’s functionality, and users had to resort to apps like HiLight Studio to unlock the LED’s full potential.

articles.body: I’ve spent years trying the latest book-style foldables, but none earned a permanent spot in my pocket once I finished testing them. Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 7 came the closest with a thin-and-light design and truly flagship specs. Unfortunately, it suffered from the same problems as every other folding phone with a squarish inner screen aspect ratio. The form factor isn’t conducive to widescreen video content, as you’ll see large black bars at the top and bottom of the folding screen. Samsung built the wide Galaxy Z Fold 8 to specifically address this pain point, and it quickly won me over. Then, something happened that I didn’t expect. I found myself using the Galaxy Z Fold 8 unfolded in portrait orientation more than landscape.

articles.body: Ridley Scott has spent nearly five decades returning to the same basic question: What does it mean to be human when the world around us stops making sense? articles.excerpt: Don't miss the best lunar eclipse until New Year's Eve 2028. Here's when to look up to catch the deep partial lunar eclipse on Aug. 27-28.
articles.body: A dramatic partial lunar eclipse will occur on Aug. 27-28, with almost the entire moon slipping into Earth's shadow. At its peak, at 12:12 a.m. EDT (0412 GMT) on Aug. 28, 96.2% of the lunar surface will be covered by Earth's dark umbral shadow, leaving only a slender portion of the moon directly illuminated by the sun. The rest of the lunar surface may take on an eerie reddish-orange hue, creating an impressive 'almost blood moon'. The eclipse will be visible from North and South America, Europe and Africa , though exactly how much you'll see will depend on your location (and clouds!). articles.title: Pluto losing its planet status may be the best thing that ever happened to solar system diversity
articles.excerpt: Unpopular opinion time, Pluto being reclassified as a dwarf planet was a great thing for our understanding of the solar system and for the former planet, too.
articles.body: Unpopular opinion time, but someone has to say it: I think Pluto being reclassified as a dwarf planet was a great thing for our understanding of the solar system and for the former planet itself. Let me try to convince you, too. First, a little background. The Pluto planet controversy began exactly 20 years ago on Aug. 24, 2006, when the International Astronomical Union (IAU) reclassified the solar system's (former) ninth planet as a dwarf planet. The reason for the change was the result of the discovery of worlds similar to Pluto in the Kuiper Belt , the ring of icy bodies and debris extending out beyond the orbit of Neptune. It suddenly became necessary to determine if these bodies are planets or whether the definition of what a planet is needs to be reshaped.

articles.body: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is encapsulated within the payload fairing at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida, ahead of mating to a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket for launch. Credit: NASA/Sydney Rohde (Rocz) Coverage plans are ready for NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope prelaunch and launch activities. Roman is NASA’s next-generation observatory designed to explore some of the universe’s biggest mysteries, including dark energy. NASA and SpaceX are targeting Roman’s liftoff for no earlier than 7:26 a.m. EDT Sunday, Aug. 30, aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket from Launch Complex 39A at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Launch coverage begins at 6:20 a.m. Live coverage of these events will stream through a variety of platforms.

articles.title: 'Ghosts of Mars' at 25: Are we any closer to living on the Red Planet? We asked the experts
articles.excerpt: John Carpenter's 'Ghosts of Mars' explored a future where Mars is terraformed, but is it closer to becoming a reality? We spoke to the experts to find out.
articles.body: In August 2001, filmmaker John Carpenter said "Boo!" and unleashed " Ghosts of Mars " on the world. While not one of Carpenter's most revered works, it's still a neat sci-fi horror movie in which Mars has been terraformed – 84% terraformed to be exact – and inhabited by humans. Plus, it has Jason Statham and Ice Cube in it, so it's automatically 99% better than all other movies ever made. Now, the action takes place at Shining Canyon, a remote mining outpost on Mars that has a gritty wild west/Mad Max-ness vibe; it's cold, harsh, and so so so so soooooo dusty – not exactly a dream home location. Then there's the whole "scary horde possessed by ancient extraterrestrial evil spirits trying to kill you" thing.
